segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Forty-One. If a parallelogram shares the same base with a triangle and lies in the same parallels, the parallelogram is double the triangle. Let parallelogram A B C D share the same base B C with triangle E B C, and let them lie in the same parallels B C and A E. We prove that parallelogram A B C D is double triangle B E C.

segments.text: Triangles A B C and E B C stand on the same base B C and lie in the same parallels B C and A E. By Proposition Thirty-Seven, triangle A B C is equal in area to triangle E B C. Yet by Proposition Thirty-Four, the diagonal A C bisects parallelogram A B C D, so parallelogram A B C D is double triangle A B C. Therefore parallelogram A B C D is also double triangle E B C, as was required to prove.
